references.text: Jesus confirms that He Himself is the witness, and that the Father is the second witness, expanding on the theme that His testimony is not of human origin.
Jesus claims that He knows where He comes from and where He is going, and that His testimony is true even if no one else bears witness, emphasizing independence from human confirmation.
Jesus explains that He does not speak on His own authority, but that the Father who sent Him has given Him a message, confirming that His testimony is not human.
The written testimony is true, and it is given so that you may believe, reflecting the purpose in John 5:34 that the words are given so that people may be saved.

John the Baptist comes as a witness to testify about the light, but Jesus emphasizes in 5:34 that He Himself does not need human testimony to be true, even though He uses it for the salvation of others.
